title: Ruy Lopez: Open
line: Black takes the center pawn and plays actively; White opens lines and wins the pawn back.

steps.text: The Ruy Lopez: Black asks the bishop what it will do.
The bishop steps back and White castles. Black takes the pawn on e4: this is the Open Ruy Lopez.
Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares. It attacks the pawn on e5 and opens the center while Black's king is still there.

also.f1e1: Attacking the knight with the rook is also played. This lesson pushes the pawn.

steps.text: The pawn chases your bishop. Step it back, still aimed at the pawn on f7.
steps.after: Black guards the knight with a pawn and blocks your bishop.

steps.text: Take the pawn on e5. The material is level again.
steps.after: Black's pieces stand well, but your pawn on e5 gives you space.

steps.text: Move the pawn on c2 one square. Your bishop gets a way back to c2, aimed at the king side.

also.b1d2: Attacking the knight first is also played. This lesson moves the pawn first.
also.c1e3: That is also played. This lesson moves the pawn first.

steps.text: A slip common at club level: here Black took the pawn on d4 instead of chasing the bishop. The knight on e4 now stands in front of its king.
Bring the rook to the file of the knight and the king. The knight cannot move without exposing the king.
steps.after: Black guards the knight with a pawn.

steps.text: Take back the pawn on d4. The knight on e4 is still pinned, and Black's king is stuck in the middle.
steps.after: White has the pawn back and a strong attack on the file.

summary: Black takes the pawn, White opens the center at once and wins it back. Taking a second pawn opens the file to the king.
